objective: Recover all 17 explicitly rejected high-pressure wet-heavy-oil TP-flash states without regressing the frozen 39/49/22 mainline or weakening product acceptance gates.
executive_summary: Two ordering defects were corrected. A late aqueous seed is now passed through the phase-fraction solver before final validation, and a non-equilibrium water-rich two-phase endpoint above the water critical pressure is repaired before tangent-plane stability expansion. The exact SRK/Peneloux/classic cold-start grid improves from 865/882 to 882/882 accepted states. The engineering classification above 200 bara is upgraded from partly UNVERIFIED to LIMITED, not VERIFIED, because independent boundary closure remains available only through 200 bara.
approach: The 17 failures were first frozen and classified into 10 STALLED, 5 invalid phase-removal, and 2 NOT_REQUIRED states that failed the independent fugacity gate. The high-temperature fixed residual was traced to a late aqueous seed that bypassed solveBeta. The low- and mid-temperature failures were traced to tangent-plane stability analysis being run on a non-equilibrium water-rich two-phase endpoint. The implementation changes solver ordering only; EOS parameters, damping, ridge regularization, and acceptance tolerances are unchanged.
conclusions: All 17 baseline rejects are recovered with no new failed state in the 882-point cold-start grid. The frozen 39/49/22 gates and both targeted product states pass. Numerical state solving is therefore closed for the sampled domain. High-pressure phase-envelope topology is not independently closed above 200 bara, so >200-300 bara is LIMITED rather than VERIFIED.
recommendations: Use 0.5-200 bara as VERIFIED for the exact sampled model and temperature range.
Use >200-300 bara only with the existing per-state status, material-balance, and fugacity gates until an independent high-pressure boundary is closed.
Do not generalize the repair to reactive, ionic, CPA, different-composition, or different-mixing-rule systems without separate validation.
Keep the water-critical-pressure guard; it prevents the repair path from replacing the reliable subcritical-pressure stability workflow.
